item.title: Hephaestus - SCP Concept
item.content:encoded:
Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Typical Layout (SC Procedures, Description, Addenda)

Genre: No specific genre

Elevator Pitch: The SCP (Preferably SCP-5766) is a wildfire located in Northern Norway started in late April of 2010 approximately 0.43 square kilometres in area.

Central Narrative: SCP was started in late April of 2010 at 2:00 PM during a lightning storm that had killed over 200 separate creatures including foxes, wolves, reindeer, and puffins. SCP was presumably started when a lightning strike lit several coniferous trees affected by dry-rot.

SCP was discovered by a hiker during a hike in Northern Norway. At 4pm, he noticed a large quantity of soot and smoke in the trees, a noticeable change in visibility of the area and an increased air temperature. He followed what he presumed where the smoke originated from, and unknowingly discovered SCP while the large volume of smoke in the area, however he never noticed the presence of SCP.

The Foundation was first notified of SCP from the Norwegian Government when a collection of meteorologists and climatologists noticed an unusual quantity of smoke coming from the region of the SCP’s presence. The Foundation investigated and put containment of the object into effect.

SCP began forming a local greenhouse effect across its nearby regions on the 13th of September 2012, through immense emission of Carbon Dioxide and Water Vapour, causing intense heat during the day and night hours in the region.

Attention-Grabber: This SCP is the first SCP mainly focused on wildfires.

Addenda:

  • Hephaestus is the God of Fire in Greek Mythology.

item.title: SCP Concept: Reflection
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is an anomalous event in a gas station, where if an individual looks at the bathroom's mirror for enough time they will be controlled and later killed by their reflection.

Central Narrative: An SCP Foundation Researcher is driving in his car to his house, he suddenly sees a gas station and stops there to wash his face. He enters the bathroom and begins realizing this gas station was never here before, hence why he didn't recognize it. As he was washing his face, the Researcher began looking intently at the mirror and started scratching his arm uncontrollably, grabbed his hair and breathed heavily, showing signs of paranoia, then suddenly began acting against his own will and followed his reflection's movement. After a bit, the reflection smiled and grabbed a hammer, so did the Researcher, they both swung the hammer towards the mirror, shattering it, and the Staff member dropped dead in the bathroom with multiple cuts around his body. The Foundation later found the body and started studying the SCP, theorizing it's origin and it's containment.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The gas station is often moved between places and awaits for it's next victim, and what's interesting to note is that the individual starts becoming their own reflection and begins following it's movement. It swaps the real person with the reflection, which can't escape the mirror and can only kill others.

Additional Notes: The SCP manipulates and kills people in the same way every time, however the anomaly doesn't work if multiple people are witnessing, which is why it mostly targets one or two people. After the mirror is shattered and the individual is dead, the gas station will move locations which leaves the body on the ground in the location of the murder and rebuilds the mirror instantly.

item.title: Don't go where the stars are nebulas
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an anomaly that alters the area it's in. It's located in the desert of Barden, Utah where there's no cities. The anomaly itself is located in an abandoned factory (although the lights of it still work for some reason) and is the body of a women shielding a child in the fetal position, with the child holding a hand-made teddy bear.

show
Hide

The body however seems to send signals that are telepathic in nature. However, the only things the foundation was able to decipher said "Please help me," and "Is my son okay?"
After the Sudden appearance of the anomaly where made, the SCP foundation attempted to contain it, but it showed ineffective as any structures made to contain it where altered or removed completely.

Central Narrative: After the sudden appearance of SCP-XXXX, the SCP foundation revived reports of cars getting into accidents where the area was altered, such as boulders suddenly appearing, roads leading to giant holes, etc. The foundation investigated and found a partially working but abandoned factory that wasn't there before. They quickly shut off the road passing by the anomaly and began investigating.

Show
Hide

Explorations in the anomaly where conducted and they found out that the mother was protecting her from something, but what that something is is unknown. The factory seemed to undergo several major failures and an outside force pushing into the factory.
The alteration in the area is discovered to be SCP-XXXX changing it to fit the area of where they came from, most likely another universe or dimension.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: For readers into SCP articles with plenty of exploration logs and mystery to solve, this can be a good article for them

Additional Notes: I was considering making a "Ray Cat solution" where the scp foundation is unable to contain it entirely and instead intergrated the properties of the scp into pop-culture and warn the dangers of "where the stars turned into nebulas"

item.title: SCP Idea, needs greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This new SCP is a Euclid 5th dimensional creature that can only be seen in the 3rd dimension due to human limitations. It is a 1.8 meter tall floating polyhedron figure that vibrates faster then the human eye can see, making it look distorted (I have a drawing and a sandbox, reply and ask for this if you would like.) There is no way yet found to figure out the actual shape of this SCP, but is expected to be larger then seen. It's voice is heard from all directions within a 20 foot radius, directly speaking into the mind of the listener, not from any position.

Central Narrative: SCP was found at a crash landing like a meteorite in a redacted city in Malaysia. Inside men at the Malaysian Special Branch were alerted and sent in a MTF. In a interview( see sandbox), the interviewer was told that the SCP was on this planet to relay information about the 3rd detention as part of a "science experiment".

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP acts as a godlike creature that can absorb knowledge of people it communicates to. SCP also grows in size when matter is absorbed by it, depending on the mass of the object. SCP has the ability to lure in people to come in contact with it, seemingly unwillingly, which in turns gets absorbed by SCP to gain mass. (Interview). The SCP seems to be willing to stay in the containment, in fear of doing harm to the planet and its people, "I intend to cause no destruction, but my nature on this plane of existence is dangerous." (SCP).

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP and I was hoping that a veteran can help me make this an official SCP. Thank you guys so much for taking your time to read this!

item.title: SCP Idea: Stuffed animals
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Drama/Emotional.

Elevator Pitch: 2 plush puppies that come to life whenever a child is nearby. They act like regular puppies, but very aggressive towards any adult with a lab coat. They have no way of harming anyone.

Central Narrative: The puppies have the consciousness of 2 young kids. The kids and one of their parents were on the brink of death after an accident. While in the hospital, a doctor was testing to see if they could transfer consciousness into anything other than a computer, and used the family as test subjects. It is implied that the near-dead parent is somewhere, but has gone missing. The 2 kids are all the Foundation has so far.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I intend this to be a slow burn, of sorts. The final addendum will reveal the full story, but before that, there are clues. The pups will be afraid of the researchers and would try to protect any kid from them, one will react to their human name, they'll try to get people they trust to follow them somewhere, etc. It's a little mystery before the end of the article.

Additional Notes: While the pups wouldn't be able to talk, I am thinking about having an "interview" log of sorts, where they'd be able to point to words on a board and communicate that way. I'm not sure if that's a good idea though, so any insight will help with that!

item.title: Re: Help with posting a comment
item.content:encoded:
A last question: Is any of this actually necessary in writing SCP articles and tales?

Not particularly! Many popular articles, past and present, use very limited formatting to tell their story; see how SCP-076 and SCP-5366 both have extremely basic designs. If you understand the basics of what's explained in Wiki Syntax, you'll be fine.

Honestly? The best advice I can give you is just to find a page with formatting you like, and then take that formatting for your own use. I did this all the time when I first started writing and I didn't understand what code meant; eventually it kinda rubs off on you. You can find the page source of a page by scrolling to the bottom, clicking "+ Options", and then clicking "Page Source".

For example, if you wanted to use the black-border divs in SCP-3000, you could check the page source and find that the code is…

 [[div style="float: center; border: solid 4px #444444; width: 570px; padding: 1px 15px; margin: 10px 10px 10px 40px; box-shadow: 2px 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.2);"]] text [[/div]]

… and apply that it your article, and even make some changes if you want.

I will also be copying your reply in a word document to use for later, if that is fine with you.

No worries! Feel free to reach out if you have further tech questions, I'm happy to help.

item.title: SCP: The Tooth Jar (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • SCP-XXXX is an ordinary looking empty glass jar
  • If a human subject is eating a meal within a short distance radius around SCP-XXXX, teeth will appear inside the food
  • Putting these teeth inside the jar will transmute them into radioactive coins
+ Show more
- Show less

Central Narrative:

SCP-XXXX is a ordinary looking glass jar that can be opened or closed with a metallic lid. Manufacturing codes engraved at the bottom of SCP-XXXX suggest it originally was a jar of Dijon mustard.

Eating solid food within a 20 meter radius around SCP-XXXX will have the following effect occur: after chewing four to five times, the subject will bite on a small human tooth, that was not initially present in the food. This tooth, called SCP-XXXX-1, matches the DNA of the subject that bit on it, although no loss of tooth is observed on the subject.

This phenomenon can be repeated. An instance of SPC-XXXX-1 will appear in the consumed food every four to five mastications, and this will always result in the subject biting onto it, leading to possible mouth injuries if unprepared.
Every time an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 is created, its mass is substracted from the subject's bone mass. Excessive repetition of the phenomenon on the same subject will result in the onset of bone-related diseases, such as osteoporosis.

Placing instances of SCP-XXXX-1 into SCP-XXXX, closing it with the lid, and breaking all visual contact with it allow for the transmutation event to take place instantly.
The transmutation event can occur only if no human person or camera has a visual contact with SCP-XXXX. The transmutation effectively replaces all instances of SCP-XXXX-1 with coins, referred to as SCP-XXXX-2.

Instances of SCP-XXXX-2 look identical to coins of the French Franc currency. Composition and engravings on the surface matches that of regular coins melted in 1982.
All instances of SCP-XXXX-2 are highly radioactive, averaging 80 μSv/h, warranting their rapid disposal.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: Have you ever bitten on your own dislodged tooth while eating, when you were a child? It's not the most pleasant of sensations. This SCP also twists the tale of the tooth fairy in a SCP-esque fashion.

item.title: Re: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
I ultimately came down to a no-vote (neutral vote) on this.

I think the main problem here is that the core concept leans heavily on a few site cliches, and doesn't do enough to build beyond that. As a fan of technical scips, the tight tone and some interesting nuances to the effect helped sell me a bit on the idea (the experiment logs in particular have some good moments of black humor and creepiness), but ultimately there's no moment where I find myself saying "oh?…ooohh…" or staring at the screen processing the full ramifications of what I just read.

I'm not saying this can't work, but it might be one to put on the back-burner while you work on something more off the beaten trail; some of the best twists come from letting an idea sit for a while until you get one of those "Oh duh, that's what I should do!" moments.

item.title: Re: Help with posting a comment
item.content:encoded:
Generally, you're not gonna need to mess with the toolkit buttons at the top of the text area all that much, if you're just leaving a normal comment somewhere.

8) how do I link another article in my comment?

This is really the only one of your questions that might come up with some regularity. Linking syntax is explained in Wiki Syntax, and looks like this: [URL-name what you want the link to say]. For example, that link to Wiki Syntax could be written as [http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/wiki-syntax Wiki Syntax].

+ Click for answers to your other questions
– hide block

1) what's a heading level 1 (largest)?

What it sounds like, basically: it's a heading for a particular section. You can see them at play on the U.S. Department of Education's website — see how all the lines that say "Press Releases", "Betsy DeVos", "Featured", etc. are all a different font and a larger size? Those are headers in action.

2) what's a div block element?

Webpages like to section everything on the page into rectangles; you can see that in the general layout of this site pretty clearly, specially the side-bar to your left. divs are those rectangles, and putting one in your comment can let you do some cooler formatting.

For example:

The background of this div is the color salmon.

And:

This is a more advanced use of divs.

This is a pretty basic feature of HTML, and it's not something you really need to worry about all that much for casual site use.

3) what's a clear floats (both)?

Sometimes, to get more varied web-design, pages "float" divs beside each other, as you can again see on the U.S. Department of Education's website. These don't have borders or background colors, but the "Press Releases" and "Betsy Devos" sections are divs, and they're next to each other. The former is floated left, the later floated right.

Clear floats (both) just means that any part of the page after that isn't going to start floating in the empty space between those two elements; it acts as an invisible barrier that stops floating.

4) what's a table wizard?

That's just Wikidot's little tool for setting up a table, like this:

header header header
cell-content cell-content cell-content
cell-content cell-content cell-content

5) what's a table of contents?

That's a list of links on a page that lets users quickly navigate between headers; it doesn't work in comments, but you can see it in use here at the bottom of the "MOBILE TASK FORCES" div.

6) what's a code block/ code block wizard?

That lets you show off code as plaintext. For instance, here's that more advanced div I showed off earlier:

 [[div style="border: 6px double black; width: 50%; margin: auto; text-align: center; padding: 0 15px; border-radius: 5px;"]] This is a more advanced use of divs. [[/div]]

The code wizard also lets you select what type of programming language the code is, which colors in particular elements for increased readability.

7) what's a raw text - escape parsing?

That's just a way of telling wikidot, "hey, display this as plaintext". I used this when I was explaining links to you above, so you could see the syntax.

Lastly, I am mostly reaching out for step-by-step tutorials any of you might know and would be willing to share on formatting.

Most of this is just usual Wikidot stuff that's explained in their documentation. I self-taught CSS and HTML by writing here, but I know Khan Academy has a pretty good, free-to-learn course on the matter. W3Schools also has an exhaustive list of CSS properties and explanations thereof, which I reference frequently.

But again, if you're just reading and commenting, a lot of this is just for fun.

– hide block

Hopefully that helps!

item.title: Re: Monstrous teeth
item.content:encoded:
Hey there. I'm a newbie here so I don't know much, but after looking through this Drafts Critique forum for a while, I noticed a rule that the admins keep posting.

Then again you said you are not a first-time author, so I don't know if this applies to you, but here is the comment I copied from a senior member:

Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

You already have a thread for this here: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13855933/therapist-based-scp so I suggest reaching out to reviewers to ask them to look at that thread so you can obtain the necessary greenlights to get draft critique here.

That's about it.

Also, my personal opinion on this SCP: it would scare the living cr*p out of me. However, I do not understand the reason for it being Keter class. It does not kill or otherwise harm SCP-XXXX-2. You did mention at the end that he is not dangerous but his modus operandi is disturbing, however I would still, personally, make it a Euclid class.

Also, what would happen exactly if it were not allowed to treat a D-class daily? How would it try to breach containment?

Lastly, I don't think the Foundation would go out of their way to call it Dr SCP-XXXX simply because of it requesting it.

As it's stated in the How to Write an SCP page: Don't write its containment procedures to essentially be "Give it What it Wants". The Foundation is not a hotel, it is a prison.

Thus, I highly doubt the Foundation would grant this SCP's request to be called Doctor.

item.title: Re: Does this SCP exist already?
item.content:encoded:
There are a LOT. SCP-3999 is the most extreme, but SCP-1893 and most other things with the pataphysical tag either affect the document or are the document in some way. Allison Eckhart is another Allison Eckhart of the kind of Allison Eckhart you’re talking about, in that it changes its own Allison Eckhart (well, not directly, but the document is still screwy because of the anomaly’s influence). SCP-2343 is a reality bender (or ancient Egyptian god, whatever) who alters his own documentation. SCP-732 is some kind of $&@INCREDIBLY AWESOME AND HANDSOME!!!111!11&@&& memetic entity that infests digital documents and replaces parts of it with self insert l33tspeak. I also affect my document, hilariously. So yeah, it’s been done many times. Doesn’t mean you can’t do it again, but you’ll need to do something special to make it stand out.

You do not recognize the bodies in the water.

Very strange that only O5 council members can access the SCP's containment

Level 5 security clearances are given to the highest-ranking administrative
personnel within the Foundation and grant effectively unlimited access to all
strategic and otherwise sensitive data. Level 5 security clearances are typically
only granted to O5 Council members and selected staff.

This sentence doesn't make sense to me. Is it a crystal with a

The description is simply put, painful to get through. I'd say you could cut

item.title: SCP Idea: Never Ending Creativity (Seeking Green lights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Other (Mystery)

Page Layout (Optional): A slightly more modernized version of a regular file entry/document, with the tests and interviews all in a recording log form.

Elevator Pitch:

  • This SCP looks different to everyone who sees it.
  • Once someone sees it, they always see it that way.
  • Once seen it can never be forgotten not even by the top class amnestics.

Central Narrative: The artist who made the painting had went missing a few months before the object was found. Whoever made it and it's purpose is unknown. It may have a pocket dimension and that's where it gets all of it's "forms" from. This SCP has fooled the foundation for years, got a little carried away one time and was reclassified and containment procedures became way more strict. It also knows more than anyone thinks, It knows stuff that seems like it was just made up. But most of the time it actually happened.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP was found in an abandoned house, full of pictures and drawings. It seemed to belong to a an enthusiastic artist. Despite it's very silent nature, it has been proven to be sentient. When the SCP rarely does talk, it doesn't talk much and keeps to itself. It's more cunning and deceptive than some top deception artists. It's like creativity itself, but it is not the easiest to persuade to do anything willingly.

Additional Notes: I'd like more help with the Hook/Attention Grabber and Central Narrative. I am not too good at figuring out what info should go in which spot, so I'd like help with that.

item.title: The Serpent
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a giant snake in golden skin that has ability to grow an unknown type of plants in surrounding area that is capable of producing any life form/part of the life form based on the DNA and the nutrients that SCP-XXXX consumed (the DNA can only be stored inside the SCP for a few months). It is capable of twisting and manipulating the DNA although it's not good at doing so. After the incident, the SCP foundation found out that SCP-XXXX can also manipulate its own organic structure and DNA. Because of experiments with many type of life form and other anomolies SCP-XXXX became highly sapient with some other abilities:
• When in an effective range any action that is carried out with the intent to kill SCP-XXXX is impossible to do
• Ability to read anyone mind in a range
• After self-cannibalism, SCP-XXXX heal, slightly change appearance and create time distortion (time moves unevenly, some areas slow, some fast and even stopped or skip appart. Seemingly it can control all of that) around itself for a few hours

Central Narrative: due to the nature of SCP-XXXX , the foundation decided to use it to create loyal anomolies that can help the foundation in containing other SCPs. The foundation tried to understand and control SCP-XXXX. After many attempt, the foundation aware of the changes in behavior and decided to cancel the project. A failed termination attempt caused a severe damage to the site, for some reason SCP-XXXX stayed inside a site and created a person that could understand it. He later become a researcher level 3 and one of the lead researcher in containing SCP-XXXX

Hook/Attention-Grabber: it is interesting to think about the possibility of what can this SCP do, what happens if it interact with other organic SCPs. The other thing that make this special is that the contradictions between the fact that this SCP poses a huge threat to humanity and the fact that it needs the foundation

item.title: A Day in the Life *Seeking Greenlights*
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: Tale.

Genre: Bureaucratic slice-of-life.

Page Layout: Presented as an in-universe section of the Quarterly Foundation Budgetary Assessment.

Elevator Pitch: Accountants and actuaries would be a vital part of the Foundation infrastructure that is often handwaved away. This tale would serve to highlight their role in the background of the narrative, considering the cost and risk-benefit analyses inherent in any large-scale organization.

Central Narrative: Menial workers (janitors, maintenance technicians, etc.) in contact with various low-danger anomalies begin to display mental ailments not consistent with any prior anomalous traits. Pre-existing case studies of various examples are presented. An across-the-board complete neurological and psychiatric evaluation is proposed in order to fully grasp the scope of the issue. O5 Command agrees, but also prescribed an analysis of replacing potentially compromised staff with genetically engineered automata.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The format itself is different than what typically appears; the concern for fiscal resources is also generally not present in-universe. Additionally, describing the toll that most "normal" Foundation staff must pay in their line of duty: having to constantly refer to a rose bush by a different, feminine name; be inundated with the color red, not only at work, but in the rest of their lives; even the burden of having to clean the tank of a sea slug that speaks to you and claims to be a renowned naturalist. Finally, the concept of replacing people with organic AIs is presented with the cold, classically-Foundation disregard for the livelihood and general concern of the people.

Here are my thoughts on 5944;

Line by Line
Line by Line

openable only to on-site staff with Level 5 clearance or above

Very strange that only O5 council members can access the SCP's containment seeing how they generally aren't supposed to come in contact with anomalies.

SCP-5944 is a tactile cognitohazard in the form of an anomalous translucent crystal.

This sentence doesn't make sense to me. Is it a crystal with a cognitohazardous effect, because this sentence seems to imply that the crystal itself is like the physical embodiment of the cognitohazard or something?

General Thoughts
General Thoughts

The description is simply put, painful to get through. I'd say you could cut at least half of those words out and it'd still make just as much sense. There is no hook; some kind of mystery in the conprocs to pull you through all of that. By the second paragraph, I already understood what it was. None of the rest was necessary.

The anomaly itself is generic and boring. It's a crystal that turns people into zombies, and this skip does nothing interesting with it. The interview and experiment logs all blur together. It's just zombies being zombies. It's exactly what I expected based on the description. There is no twist or subversion. It doesn't lead anywhere. I suppose the final addendum is supposed to be some kind of conclusion but I honestly have no idea what it means.

I can't really suggest specific changes because I think the idea itself needs major reworking. I recommend checking out the Ideas Forum if you want some advice from experienced authors.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight): Elaine of Astolat's Curse
item.content:encoded:
You may want to look at my answer to JamaisJ to get more of information.

But the whole setup of interviewing the anomaly and then she drops some important information (amidst a backstory about shadowy kidnappers) seems constructed, and more importantly, lacking in conflict. There aren't really stakes involved here that make this reveal dramatic.

I would have added this in but I wasn't sure how important the discovery was. My idea as that SCP-XXXX was discovered in Farringford House in the 40s during its hand over to the British Holiday Estates Ltd. Upon SCP-XXXX's discovery, the first recorded SCP-XXXX-1 occurred. SCP-XXXX was later taken in by the Foundation for research and containment. During the interview, we learn more about these mutilations and scars and discover these 'kidnappers' weren't kidnappers in reality. They were her guards. They were essentially doing what the foundation is currently doing. Keeping SCP-XXXX out of sight and ensuring SCP-XXXX-1 didn't happen.

I encourage you to also implement a more standard, uh, rising-action/climax format as well.

What I'm planning in the climax is made the dramatic ending you'd like. The coating on SCP-XXXX's eyelids is also decaying, all be it slower than regular reflective surfaces but still at a measurable rate. This means that at some point, SCP-XXXX's coating will stop working. Then the problems for the Foundation begin. How will they deal with her need for blinking or sleeping? Blinking the could manage but sleeping would be harder. She may not age but she can still die of other means. Really, the moment her eyelid coating ceases working, the likelihood of SCP-XXXX-1 occurring increases.

I meant to bring this up, but how involved is this reference going to be? It seems like a throwaway atm, with no purpose but gesturing towards a popular poem as an inspiration. Is there some story going on about her being Tennyson's inspiration?

This ties into her discover. As she was discovered at Farringford House, there is a good chance she was connected to Tennyson as the Tennyson family owned Farringford House until the 40s. My idea is that Tennyson and his Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood (real thing btw) may have either be involved with SCP-XXXX's creation or were just her caretakers. Also, SCP-XXXX's imprisonment and abilities may have taken its toll on the Brotherhood. SCP-XXXX could be why Tennyson's brother, Edward Tennyson ended up in a private institution. Tennyson wrote The Lady of Shallot as a means of dealing with all the horrible things they do to SCP-XXXX. The poem just acts as further evidence of her involvement with Tennyson. Now that you point it out, however, I do think that the poem is more of an additional note than an actual hook. The hook is more likely her decaying eyelid coating and the fact that the SCP-XXXX's situation and containment may get worse and harder to control.
